title: Evaluating the Capabilities of LLMs for Persuasive Dialogue
abstract: arXiv:2608.29738v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate apparently highly persuasive text, but does sounding persuasive mean arguing well? We introduce \textsc{Persuasio}, a multi-agent dialogue platform grounded in a formal argumentation-based theory of persuasion dialogues that adjudicates logical winners during free-text debates. Using this system, we generated 192 debates on a UK political topic between humans and LLMs, and evaluated 22 interlocutors through both automated adjudication and 9,702 crowdsourced pairwise judgements across 1{,}386 annotation instances. We observed a consistent decoupling between subjective and formal persuasiveness: LLMs dominated the subjective ranking yet performed substantially worse under argumentation-theoretic adjudication, where humans remained competitive. translated_title: 评估大语言模型在说服性对话中的能力
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）能够生成表面上极具说服力的文本，但听起来有说服力是否意味着论证得好？我们提出了Persuasio，一个基于形式化论证理论的说服对话多智能体对话平台，能够在自由文本辩论中裁决逻辑上的胜者。利用该系统，我们生成了192场关于英国政治话题的人机辩论，并通过自动化裁决以及涵盖1,386个标注实例的9,702条众包成对评判，对22位参与者进行了评估。我们观察到主观说服力与形式说服力之间存在持续的脱钩现象：LLM在主观排名中占据主导地位，但在论证理论裁决下表现明显较差，而人类仍保持竞争力。多智能体和检索增强变体进一步扩大了这种分歧。这些发现揭示了修辞流畅性与形式论证能力之间的系统性差距。
tldr: 该研究通过形式化论证理论评估发现，大语言模型虽然在主观上听起来极具说服力，但在严谨的论证能力上仍落后于人类，揭示了修辞流畅性与逻辑论证质量之间的系统性差距。
en_tdlr: LLMs may sound highly persuasive, but they perform substantially worse than humans under formal argumentation-theoretic adjudication, revealing a systematic gap between rhetorical fluency and sound argumentation.
